summary: Built the /blog/ section (one JSON file per post in content/blog, auto-listed and added to the sitemap and nav), the admin-only automation activity page at #/admin/activity backed by a protected API, and AUTOMATION.md for other agents.
Built a corrected Mosconi Cup graphic (accurate 9-ball rack) and pushed it, but the site did not deploy it (URL still 404 after ~15 min), so it was NOT posted to Instagram.
Top trend: the 2026 Mosconi Cup (Team USA vs Team Europe) is Nov 27-30 at the Caribe Royale in Orlando, Florida; qualification details were still being announced.

Made and checked a Mosconi Cup Orlando graphic but did NOT post to Facebook or Instagram: the website has not deployed any of the recent pushes (the /blog/ page and both images return 404 after 20+ minutes), so there is no public image URL. GitHub says the repository moved to klboy87/Billiardactiontime, which may have broken the Railway auto-deploy link - please check Railway.

Skipped posting to Facebook and Instagram again: the website still has not deployed the pushes since about 17:26 UTC (the /blog/ page and the social images still return 404), so there is no public image URL. Railway auto-deploy needs checking.

Fixed the stalled deploys: the live Railway service (project spectacular-vitality, which holds billiardactiontime.com, the env vars and the database volume) had not deployed since Nov 6 because its GitHub link broke when the repo was renamed. Reconnected it to klboy87/Billiardactiontime main; the latest commit is now live and /blog/ and the social images return 200.
Posted the Mosconi Cup Orlando (Nov 27-30, Team USA vs Team Europe) graphic to the Billiard Action Time Facebook page and to Instagram.

Top trends: (1) 2026 Mosconi Cup in Orlando Nov 27-30 with Ruijsink captaining Team USA and an ESPN+/WNT TV streaming deal; (2) World Nineball Tour season-closing events and Mosconi qualification; (3) fans looking for beginner-friendly explanations. Chose a 9-ball rules explainer since Mosconi news was already covered today.

Shared the 9-ball rules article on both Facebook Pages and Instagram.

The Windsor.ai analytics and Railway connectors failed to connect in this review, so I could not measure which posts performed best. No repo fixes were needed.
Share the Mosconi Cup countdown and poll posts in 2-3 billiards Facebook groups and ask friends to like both Pages; early reach is what trains the algorithm.
Reconnect the Windsor.ai and Railway connectors so the review routine can see real performance data and deploy status.
Send a few photos or short clips from a local tournament; real-life photos usually beat graphics on Facebook and Instagram.
